## SuperSubtitler 0.2.0 — now with a window

**Download both files into one folder:** `SuperSubtitlerGUI.exe` (the window) and `SuperSubtitler.exe` (the engine it drives). The console tool works on its own exactly as before.

### 🖥️ New: SuperSubtitlerGUI
- Drag and drop files or whole folders, every option as a switch, live progress per file and on the taskbar button.
- Track choice with tick boxes ("use for all files" remembers it by language), language questions as one-click buttons.
- Pages for **Merge** (video + audio/subtitle files → `.joined.mkv`) and **Split** (every channel as a WAV, to find the voice; then pick the **audio channel**).
- **Settings** built from `SuperSubtitler_Config.ini` itself — values are checked before they are saved, **Restore defaults** brings back the standard settings and cleaner list.

### ✨ Console tool
- **All questions come first:** languages are detected for the whole batch before the long part starts — no more waiting for Enter at file 7 in the night.
- New flags: `-auto`, `-force`, `-out:FOLDER`, `-nowait`, `-setup`, `-nomerge`, `-json`, `-version`; exit codes 0/1/2.
- The first-run setup shows real progress (MB, MB/s).
- Fixes: file names with `[brackets]` were done again and again; a closed input could hang the language question; recent PyAV releases broke every fresh install.

### 📌 The same tested runtime for everyone
Python 3.12.10, pip, every Python package incl. CUDA, FFmpeg 8.1.2 and the speech models are pinned to exact versions and checked against their SHA-256 — fetched from this project's own [`runtime-v1` mirror](https://github.com/burnersen/SuperSubtitler/releases/tag/runtime-v1) first. FFmpeg is now SuperSubtitler's own lean LGPL build (25 MB) made from the official source. Existing installs switch to this set once on their first start (existing models are reused when they match).

### 📜 Now open source under the GPLv3
From 0.2.0 on, SuperSubtitler and its window are free software under the GNU GPL, version 3 only — free for everyone, at home or at work.

The exes are not code-signed; Windows SmartScreen may warn — "More info" → "Run anyway". Built by GitHub Actions from this tag.
